answer.label: Not her exact words — a paraphrase of Mother Teresa
answer.authorDates: 1910–1997 · Roman Catholic nun · founder of the Missionaries of Charity
answer.sourceLine: The sentiment is authentically Mother Teresa’s, but this precise wording is a paraphrase. Her own Mother Teresa Center ↗ lists “Not all of us can do great things. But we can do small things with great love” among “significantly paraphrased versions… not her authentic words.” The documented, sourced form reads: “Don’t look for big things, just do small things with great love…the smaller the thing, the greater must be our love.”

author.name: Mother Teresa
author.heading: About Mother Teresa
author.metaLine: 1910–1997 · Roman Catholic nun · founder of the Missionaries of Charity
author.bio: Born Anjezë Gonxhe Bojaxhiu in Skopje in 1910, Mother Teresa founded the Missionaries of Charity in Calcutta in 1950 and spent her life serving the poorest of the poor. She won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 and was canonized as Saint Teresa of Calcutta in 2016. Her spirituality of small, hidden acts of love — echoing St. Thérèse of Lisieux’s “Little Way” — is the genuine root of this quotation, even where the popular phrasing is not her exact words.

misattribution.heading: A real thought, a rewritten line
misattribution.intro: This is one of the most-shared “Mother Teresa” quotes on the internet — and the sentiment truly is hers. But the exact popular wording has been smoothed and rephrased over time, to the point that her own center disowns it as verbatim.

items.why: Her official Mother Teresa Center ↗ lists “Not all of us can do great things. But we can do small things with great love” among lines that are “significantly paraphrased versions or personal interpretations of statements Mother Teresa made; they are not her authentic words.”
Outlets from Goodreads ↗ (which itself tags it “paraphrased”) to America ↗ present it as a motto without any primary citation, speech, or page reference.

misattribution.truthLine: The genuine, documented wording is “Don’t look for big things, just do small things with great love…the smaller the thing, the greater must be our love,” recorded in Come Be My Light (2007) ↗ — the idea is hers; the tidy internet phrasing is not.

context.heading: Why this line took on a life of its own
lead: Mother Teresa’s whole spirituality was built on the ‘Little Way’ of St. Thérèse of Lisieux — the conviction that ordinary, hidden acts, done with love, matter more than grand achievements. She said versions of this idea often, which is exactly why a clean, quotable paraphrase spread so easily and now appears on posters, mugs, and graduation cards worldwide.

The trouble is that the neat symmetrical wording people share is a later smoothing of what she actually said. Recognizing that doesn’t diminish the sentiment — it simply keeps the attribution honest, which her own religious order takes care to do.
context.pull: The idea is hers. The polished sentence is the internet’s.
